review.author: Codex
review.method: Manual source inspection by the coding agent at the pinned commit; no target code or tests executed.

grading.method: Manual evaluation rubric; no automatic score or quality gate has been run.
grading.per_question: Require each required claim with relevant evidence and reject listed contradictions. Record partial answers and unsupported claims separately.
grading.citation_integrity: Hash/span verification confirms citation identity and bounds only, not claim entailment.

required_claims.claim: fetch forwards the original Request, environment, execution context, and request.method into private dispatch.

After the HEAD special case, dispatch derives a path, matches method/path through the router, then constructs Context with matchResult, environment, execution context, and the not-found handler. Context starts unfinalized and lazily constructs its request wrapper.
Exactly one match invokes the single handler directly. Other match counts use compose, await completion, check finalization, and return context.res or route a caught error through handleError.

reject_if_claimed: All requests always use compose.
All failures including getPath/router.match failures are enclosed by the composed-dispatch catch.

required_claims.claim: HEAD recursively dispatches with the matching method argument GET, then creates a new Response with null body and the GET-dispatch response as its initialization.
The original Request object is passed through; this code does not clone it or change request.method to GET. This is a routing-method override plus response-body removal.

reject_if_claimed: HEAD has a wholly independent handler pipeline here.
The response body from GET is retained.
The Request visible to handlers is rewritten to method GET.

required_claims.claim: Composition is bypassed when matchResult[0].length equals one; the handler receives a next callback that awaits notFoundHandler and assigns c.res. Synchronous invocation errors use handleError.

The async branch is selected by instanceof Promise. A truthy resolved response is returned; otherwise finalized c.res is used, or notFoundHandler runs. Promise rejection is caught and passed to handleError.

The synchronous branch returns res with nullish-coalescing fallback to notFoundHandler; it does not consult c.finalized before falling back. Thus a synchronous handler assigning c.res but returning undefined is not handled like a Promise resolving undefined.

reject_if_claimed: Sync and async undefined results use identical fallback logic.
Every arbitrary thenable is explicitly treated as a Promise by this branch.

required_claims.claim: In compose, absence of a handler invokes onNotFound only when the context is unfinalized and that callback is supplied. A truthy result is assigned to context.res, which finalizes the context.

A handler that stops without returning a response or finalizing context does not automatically advance to the no-handler branch. Dispatch checks the resulting composed context, throws an Error if unfinalized, and passes it to handleError.

Default not-found behavior produces status 404; the default generic error path produces status 500, with a special getResponse case. These are configurable handlers, so those statuses are not universal guarantees.
The separate single-handler path has its own response fallback; it is not the composed finalization check. Merely reading c.res lazily creates a response but does not set finalized.

reject_if_claimed: A missing returned response always means 404.
Every request without an explicit returned response fails.
Reading Context.res necessarily finalizes it.

required_claims.claim: Each composed invocation starts with index -1 and dispatch(0). A selected middleware updates context.req.routeIndex and receives a next closure dispatching i+1.

Dispatch awaits each handler. Middleware that awaits next resumes its code after the downstream promise settles, allowing before/after nesting. A handler must invoke next to advance; the loop does not advance automatically.
At exactly middleware.length, the optional outer next callback can run; otherwise the absent-handler branch may invoke onNotFound.

reject_if_claimed: All middleware runs automatically regardless of next.
Code after await next runs before downstream completion.

required_claims.claim: The invocation-scoped index records the highest entered dispatch position. dispatch rejects with an Error when i <= index before selecting or invoking that position again.

Calling the same supplied next more than once leads to that guard; the guard is inside an async function, so the call yields a rejected promise. If the calling handler awaits or returns it, an enclosing dispatch catch can send the Error to onError.
The guard should not be described as an uncaught exception in every case: handler catching, supplied error handling, and whether promises are awaited affect propagation.

reject_if_claimed: A second next call silently reruns downstream middleware.
The error handler can never intercept this guard error.

required_claims.claim: Compose catches handler invocation/rejection. An instanceof Error value with onError sets context.error, awaits the error handler, and marks isError after it succeeds.

Non-Error thrown values, or Error values without onError, are rethrown by this catch. A failing onError is not caught again by that same catch; an enclosing upstream dispatch may catch the propagation.

A truthy error-handler response may replace context.res even if already finalized, because isError permits assignment. Hono dispatch handleError similarly delegates only Error instances and rethrows other values.

reject_if_claimed: All thrown values are converted to Error objects.
Providing onError handles every possible thrown value.
Error-handler output can never replace a finalized response.

required_claims.claim: Returning without invoking next stops downstream dispatch along that path; dispatch awaits the handler result and then considers assigning it to context.res.

A truthy result is assigned only while context.finalized is false or isError is true. A normal returned response therefore does not overwrite an already-finalized response through this compose assignment.

Context.res assignment updates the stored response and sets finalized true; existing response headers can be carried into the replacement, with special content-type and set-cookie behavior. Reading the getter alone does not finalize.
Middleware after await next can still run during upstream unwinding; stopping further downstream dispatch does not erase the upstream stack.

reject_if_claimed: Returning a response automatically calls the remaining middleware.
A returned response always overwrites Context.res.
No upstream middleware code runs after an early response.
